meta.description: Every 10 minutes, asks Igor whether any unhandled mail has arrived from @tdv.org. The scan is pure Gmail REST through Mark VI's own Google connection — no model, no tokens. SPEDA is only triggered when a message actually matches, and the handled mail is labelled SPEDA-Seen afterwards so it never fires twice. Import into n8n, check the domain in the scan node, activate.

nodes.name: Every 10 minutes
nodes.notes: Mail arrives at any hour, so this runs around the clock — 144 scans a day, each one HTTP request and zero tokens. Widen to */30 if you want it lazier; the SPEDA-Seen label means a longer gap only delays the push, it never loses a message.

nodes.name: Igor: scan tdv.org mail
nodes.notes:
THE CHEAP HALF. Igor runs `from:tdv.org -label:SPEDA-Seen newer_than:2d` against the owner's Gmail via the connection already set up in Settings ▸ Google Workspace, then re-checks every hit's From header against the domain properly (Gmail's from: is a fuzzy token match — it also hits display names and lookalikes). No LLM is involved, so a poll that finds nothing costs nothing.

domain is the only field worth changing. Subdomains count (burs@mail.tdv.org); nottdv.org does not.

newer_than_days is a floor, not the dedup mechanism — the SPEDA-Seen label is. It exists so a fresh watch does not fire on years of archived mail on its first tick.

neverError: a 401/5xx must not mark the run failed and spam the error workflow every 10 minutes. The response is inspected in the gate below instead.

nodes.name: Gate
nodes.notes:
The cost boundary. Everything downstream of this node spends money; everything upstream does not. A Code node that returns [] is used rather than an IF node on purpose — far fewer schema surfaces to get wrong across n8n versions, and it stops the branch outright.

store.broken lives in the workflow's static data, so the edge-trigger survives between runs.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ ({ "payload": { "type": "watchdog", "event": "tdv_mail", "job": "tdv_mail_watch", "automation": "TDV mail watch", "source": "gmail", "domain": "tdv.org", "count": $json.count, "messages": $json.messages, "intent": $json.alert ? ("Your TDV mail watch cannot read Gmail right now (status: " + $json.status + ", detail: " + $json.detail + "). Tell the owner in one short line that the watch is blind and Google likely needs reconnecting in Settings. Do not call any tool — you already have everything you know.") : "New mail arrived from tdv.org. The sender, subject and body of every message are ALREADY in `messages` in this payload — do NOT call Gmail or load a toolset, you have the mail. Read it and write the owner one short push in their language: who wrote, what they actually want, and any deadline, amount or action required. One line per message if several arrived. If something needs a reply or a date on the calendar, say so plainly and offer to do it — do not do it unasked." }, "output_mode": "push" }) }}

nodes.name: Igor: trigger SPEDA
nodes.notes:
THE EXPENSIVE HALF — one agentic turn, reached only on a real hit.

The mail bodies travel in the payload, and the intent says so, so SPEDA does not spend a second round trip re-fetching what the scan already read.

No neverError here, deliberately: if this call fails the branch must die BEFORE the mark-seen node, leaving the mail unlabelled so the next poll retries it. Retries cover the 503 the trigger endpoint returns when the turn registry is at capacity.

Retarget to /trigger/sentinel (money) or another agent by editing the URL — the push is then composed in that agent's voice.

nodes.name: Igor: mark seen
nodes.notes:
Applies the Gmail label SPEDA-Seen (created on first use) to exactly the messages that were just handed to SPEDA, so the next scan skips them. Unread state is left alone — the mail still looks untouched in the inbox.

Deliberately AFTER the trigger: labelling first would lose a message whenever the notify call failed. The cost of this ordering is a possible duplicate push if the trigger succeeds and this call fails; that is the right trade.

On the watch-broken alert path message_ids is empty and this is a no-op.
